result.result:
The Master's ETA of 31 Jan 2025 11:00 UTC for Sept-Iles is consistent: at 12.5 kn the computed ETA is 31 Jan 12:18 UTC, a 1.3 h difference within the 2 h tolerance. No CP ETA notice is due: we are 4.96 days from arrival, the last notice was sent at the 5-day threshold (ETA 06:00 UTC), the next threshold is 3 days, and the ETA has moved only 5 h against the 12 h change limit; notices go to the agent.

The remarks report a main engine stop 06:10–11:40 UTC on 26 Jan (5.5 h) with 1.1 t VLSFO used. check_stoppage confirms the stop agrees with the report: 18.5 h steaming reproduces the 231.3 nm distance run. The simulated off-hire hire statement (figures made up for this simulation) deducts hire of $2,177.08 (0.2292 days at $9,500/day) and charges bunkers of $660 (1.1 t VLSFO at $600/t), $2,837.08 to the owners' account. The CP off-hire clause (NYPE 1993 clause 17 model) ceases hire for loss of time from breakdown of machinery or equipment or a similar cause, with off-hire bunkers for owners' account; choked fuel oil filters stopping the engine may fall within it, but the owner may argue the root cause is the fuel the charterer supplied — that claim is the operator's to make. The operator should decide whether to put the ship off hire for the stop and notify the owner Tormar Bulk Carriers; on a yes: (a) propose a voyage management system off-hire entry for 26 Jan 06:10–11:40 UTC, and (b) e-mail the owner's vessel technical management with the period and reason, requesting the engine log extract for the stop. The stop is explained in the remarks, so no query to the Master is needed.
